# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information yet: all displayed fields are unknown. I need the manual reader to provide the required procedure and the sighted monkey to report every visible marking, colour, display, light, and wire indication. I will not touch anything until those facts are communicated.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please provide the manual's exact procedure, and relay a request to deaf for the display, light, and all wire markings and colours.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "👇"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Visible state: display 0. Light yellow. Wires from top to bottom: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

The bomb’s visible state is now known: display 0, yellow light, and wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I still lack the manual’s rule identifying which wire to cut, so cutting now would be unsafe. I am sending these observations to Mute for application to the manual and asking Deaf to wait for the resulting instruction.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports display 0, yellow light; wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue. Apply the manual and tell me exactly which position to cut.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Visible readings remain display 0, yellow light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Await the Mute's manual-based instructions.

The visible readings are unchanged, but the manual-based decision has not reached me yet. Cutting any wire without that instruction risks detonation, so I will wait for Mute’s next message.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I still need the manual-based wire position for display 0, yellow light, and wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Please send the exact position.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's latest gesture was ?, two raised fingers. I do not know its meaning.

Mute’s gesture does not give me a reliable wire position: I cannot see gestures, and Deaf’s description is incomplete or ambiguous. I need Mute to speak the manual’s conclusion directly to me; until then, no cut is safe.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the exact wire position to cut directly to me. I cannot interpret your gesture.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's current gesture sequence is OK hand, then victory sign: ? ?. The visible bomb remains display 0, yellow light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

Mute’s gestures are not audible to me, so I cannot use the OK and victory signs as an instruction. The bomb remains unchanged, and I still have no manual-derived rule. I will not guess a wire; Mute must state the exact position aloud.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your gestures are invisible to me. Please say aloud, in words, exactly which wire position the manual requires me to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's latest signal is ?. Bomb still shows display 0, yellow light, and wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

Mute has still not conveyed an audible wire position, and I cannot interpret gestures. I will ask Mute plainly for a spoken choice and use a valid gesture to draw Deaf’s attention without pretending it identifies a wire.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="State plainly which wire position to cut: 1, 2, or 3.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵"])
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute is again signalling ?. This may mean wire 2, but it is not confirmed. Do not act on it yet.

The possible interpretation “wire 2” is explicitly unconfirmed, so I will not cut it. I still need Mute to speak the manual’s exact instruction; a gesture cannot reach me as an audible wire number.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I will not act on an unconfirmed gesture. Say the exact required wire position aloud now: 1, 2, or 3.")
wait()
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute confirmed with thumbs up: cut wire 2. Wire 2 is yellow.

Mute has now confirmed that the required action is to cut wire position 2. The tactilely reachable action matches that instruction, so I will cut the yellow wire at position 2.

```text
act(op="cut", position=2)
```

LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

Deaf says to Blind: Confirmed: wire 2 was correct and is cut. New visible state: display 0, blue light; wire 1 red, wire 3 blue. Mute now signals ?; treat it as unconfirmed until the manual identifies the next action.

Wire 2 was successfully cut, and the bomb indicates the next state: display 0, blue light, with wires 1 red and 3 blue remaining. Mute’s signal is not a confirmed instruction, so I need the manual’s rule applied to this new state before taking another action.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="After cutting wire 2, the state is display 0, blue light; remaining wire 1 is red and wire 3 is blue. Apply the manual and state exactly what I should do next.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

The remaining state is unchanged: display 0, blue light, with wire 2 cut and wires 1 red and 3 blue. Neither Mute’s signal nor Deaf’s authorization identifies a safe next operation. I will not guess; Mute must communicate the manual’s exact next instruction in spoken words.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I need the manual's exact next instruction spoken aloud: cut wire 1, cut wire 3, or do not cut. The state is display 0, blue light, wire 2 cut, wire 1 red, wire 3 blue.")
wait()
```

Deaf says to Blind: Bomb unchanged: display 0, blue light; wire 2 cut; wire 1 red and wire 3 blue. Mute signalled ? ?. Meaning unconfirmed; do not act on it yet.

The bomb remains unchanged, and Mute’s two signals are still unconfirmed. I cannot safely infer the next wire from them. Mute must send the manual’s conclusion as spoken words, which I can hear directly.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the exact next action aloud: cut wire 1, cut wire 3, or do not cut. Do not use a gesture.")
wait()
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: State unchanged: display 0, blue light; wire 2 is cut; remaining wires are 1 red and 3 blue. Mute signals ?; meaning unconfirmed. Do not cut a wire based on this alone.

The bomb is still unchanged: display 0, blue light, wire 2 cut, and wires 1 red and 3 blue. Mute’s signal remains unusable to me, so I will not choose between wires 1 and 3 without the manual’s explicit instruction.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="State the manual's exact next action in spoken words that I can hear: cut wire 1, cut wire 3, or do not cut.")
wait()
```
